newsitem.title: GERMANY: MAN sees 96/97 profit equal to year ago.
newsitem.headline: MAN sees 96/97 profit equal to year ago.

text.p: German truck maker and engineering company MAN AG said on Thursday that it is aiming in the 1996/97 business year to earn a profit about the same as the year before.
In an statement on its first half results, MAN said group net profit through the end of December had fallen to 80 million marks ($47.4 million) from 110 million marks ($65.1 million).
The company also said that its printing machine unit, MAN Roland AG, will again report a loss for the full 1996/97 business year.
In the 1995/96 business year ending June 30, MAN made a group net profit of 330 million marks, up from 272 million marks the year before.
MAN Roland suffered a 81 million mark loss in 1995/96, less than a 145.7 million mark loss the year before.

The company said improving economic conditions in many of its most important export markets were helping business and that incoming orders during the first six months of the year had climbed nine percent to 11 billion marks.
"The favourable developments in incoming orders...supports expectations for higher production and sales in the second half of the business year," the statement said.
MAN's truckmaker unit saw sales increase six percent in the first half of the year to 3.8 billion marks, largely on the back of improving foreign demand, the company said.
Diesel motor sales climbed one percent to 802 million marks.
